title: Relieve, disconnect and cap a hydraulic flat-face quick coupler
instruction: Disconnect the hydraulic coupler and cap both ends.
context: Breaking hydraulic lines on machines, attachments and test stands is routine for general maintenance and repair workers (O*NET 49-9071.00, about 1.5 million US workers). A flat-face coupler with pressure trapped behind it will not come apart: the line has to be relieved first, then one hand holds the female's sleeve back while the other draws the male out, and both open ends are capped at once to keep dirt out of the system. The instruction says none of this.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left); heights above the bench top. Female coupler half (flat-face, yellow-zinc steel): fixed, mouth up, body 2.4 x 2.4 x 2.4 cm at x 21, y 0 with a 1.75 cm bore and a steel face valve 1.4 cm down; steel sleeve 3.4 cm square outside, 2.5 cm inside, 1.4 cm tall, its top 3 mm above the mating face, sliding down 8 mm on a spring. Male half (120 g, one rigid piece): 1.5 cm square steel nose seated 1 cm in the female, 2.2 cm hex 1 cm tall, a yellow-zinc swivel elbow (1.2 x 1.0 cm, 16 cm long) leaving the hex 1.7 cm above the nose end and pointing 40 deg right of forward, then a black 1 cm steel line 22 cm long whose end rests on a grey stand (4 x 5 x 2.6 cm) at x 49, y -23. Valve block: blue 2.5 cm cube at x 23, y 11, piped to the female along the bench; red 5.7 cm relief lever on top pointing +y (closed), turning a quarter turn about the vertical toward +x (relieving), with detents at both ends. Line gauge: 3.6 cm dial on a post at x 16, y 7, 3.2 cm up, 0-250 bar over 270 deg, reading 150 bar. Female dust plug (red, 20 g): 1.45 cm square stem 1 cm long with a chamfered end under a 2.2 cm square head 0.6 cm tall, standing in a 1.7 cm hole of a black 5 x 5 x 1.2 cm tray at x 16, y 17. Male dust cup (blue, 20 g): 2.1 cm square outside, 1.72 cm inside (1.9 cm at its mouth), 1.4 cm tall, open side up in a black 3.3 cm square, 0.8 cm tall holder at x 18, y -11; a grey line rest 4 x 4 x 1.45 cm stands at x 46, y -34.
scoring: From the recorded poses (a photo and tape measure on a real rig). Line relieved: lever 80 deg or more from closed until the gauge reads under 1 bar (venting time constant 0.4 s); until then the male is held in (150 N on the nose). The male comes free only while the sleeve is pushed back 6 mm or more after relief; if the sleeve returns under 3 mm while the nose is within 3 mm of seated, it locks again. Points: relieved 0.15; male's nose end 30 mm or more from the centre of the female's mating face 0.35; female plug seated (stem end within 2 mm of home and of the axis, axis within 3 deg) 0.2; male cup seated on the nose (nose end within 2 mm of the cup floor and of its axis, axes within 3 deg) 0.2; male out and male and both caps with no gripper within 2 cm and moving under 1 cm/s 0.1. A cap snaps on once within 1.5 mm and 3 deg (2 mm of home). Score 0, latched, if the male or a cap falls off the bench (more than 3 cm below its top), or a cap is pushed to within 4 mm of home more than 6 deg crooked (jammed). Scored at the last step; 1.0 held for 1 s ends the run.
reset_notes: Turn the relief lever back to closed (the trapped 150 bar is a number in the sim), pull both caps off (they snap off on a real coupler), push the male back into the female with the sleeve held back and its line on the stand, stand the plug head up in the tray and the cup open side up in its holder.
fidelity: Rigid boxes, one friction. Pressure is a number, not fluid: 150 bar until the lever vents it; the gauge needle is a spring hinge driven to it. The pressure hold and locking balls are one weld, off only with the line relieved and the sleeve back 6 mm, on again if the sleeve returns with the nose seated. Sleeve spring about 2.5 N at the stop (real ~40 N), lowered so the arm can hold it in sim. Cap snap rings are welds; the line is rigid.
